The four kinds are: (a) SQLite Error 5, \\u0027unable to delete/modify user-function due to active statements\\u0027, thrown from SqliteConnection.CreateFunction while a store opens a connection (seen in GitHubProfileTests, ModulePrincipalApiTests, OpenPrStepTests, GatedMergeStepTests, and WorktreeReleaseTests); (b) \\u0027The process cannot access the file\\u0027 on a read of a store\\u0027s coanda.db or coanda.db-shm while that store is still open (SessionPrincipalTests after the daemon stops and before it is disposed, and ModuleSettingsTests while the node runs); (c) the TimeoutException \\u0027did not reach paused\\u0027 in FlowRunAdvancerTests; (d) \\u0027This SqliteTransaction has completed; it is no longer usable\\u0027 from SaveChangesAsync while a test node starts, together with the ObjectDisposedException the same test\\u0027s disposal then raises. Where a cause lies inside a package, the pull request names the package, its version, and the line in this repository whose call leads to it.\u0022,\u0022Each cause the pull request names has a test that fails deterministically on the commit the branch starts from and passes after the fix (by holding the finalizer thread, forcing a collection, ordering the calls, or similar). For each such test, the pull request names the platform it failed on before the fix (this Mac or a CI leg) and shows the failing output. After the fix, each such test\\u0027s class passes at least 20 consecutive runs by class filter, and the pull request gives the command and the result.\u0022,\u0022No existing test is skipped, retried, wrapped in a retry loop, given a longer wait or timeout, or moved out of parallel execution, and no existing assertion is weakened or removed. A new test that holds the finalizer thread goes in the existing non-parallel FinalizerHoldCollection, and no other non-parallel collection is added. No new call to SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools is added anywhere.\u0022,\u0022After the fix, the pull request reports at least 20 full-suite runs made one at a time on this Mac with dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build, gives how many failed, and names each failing test with the kind from the first criterion it belongs to, or says it belongs to none. No criterion requires a consecutive run of full-suite passes or a particular failure count.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Work from origin/main, which now holds pull request #76 (HomeStore, whose disposal waits for pending finalizers, and the FinalizerHold test helper with its non-parallel FinalizerHoldCollection); reuse them. The 30-run breakdown behind these kinds is in pull request #76\\u0027s description. Its run 25 also failed RepoFieldTests at Assert.Empty(runner.Commands) (RepoFieldTests.cs:108), because two git commands ran in projects/multi/repos after ForgetCommands. That failure is not SQLite and is out of scope here (a separate task covers it); the full-suite report counts it as belonging to none of the kinds.\\n\\nOn Error 5, a lead to verify, not a finding: on a normal close, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 10.0.9\\u0027s SqliteConnection.Deactivate unregisters the connection\\u0027s functions before the native connection returns to the pool. A pooled native connection still carries Weasel\\u0027s functions only when it was returned after its outer SqliteConnection was collected, which is the ReclaimLeakedConnections path, and that path also runs from SqliteConnectionPool.Clear (so ClearAllPools in a parallel run can put a leaked connection back in service). An Error 5 at open therefore points to an outer SqliteConnection collected while open with a statement still stepping, rather than to a reader left undisposed on a connection that was later closed. Every SqliteConnection this repository opens itself uses Pooling = false under using, and every Fisher session it opens is under using. The one connection in Fisher 1.27.0 not disposed in a finally is the session\\u0027s own (OwnedConnectionLifetime.ConnectionAsync), which is not synchronized against concurrent first use: two concurrent first uses of one session would each open a connection and keep only the second.\\n\\nOn the completed-transaction kind: SqliteTransaction.Commit throws \\u0027has completed\\u0027 when SQLite\\u0027s rollback hook has fired, so the transaction was rolled back underneath Fisher\\u0027s unit of work. The ObjectDisposedException in the same failure comes from the test, not the store: OpenPrStepTests disposes its node and starts another (OpenPrStepTests.cs:326-327); when that start throws, the node field is never reassigned, so the class\\u0027s DisposeAsync disposes the first node again. SoftwareNode.StartAsync (tests/Coanda.Tests/Modules/Software/SoftwareNode.cs:116-133) also leaves a started daemon running when a later step throws. Both halves are in scope.\\n\\nOn the open-store reads: both reads are in the tests themselves (SessionPrincipalTests.cs:331-334, ModuleSettingsTests.cs:206-226). On macOS, a write lock that SQLite holds on a live store refuses .NET\\u0027s shared read, while on Linux the two locks never conflict, so a deterministic test for this kind may fail only on this Mac. A fix that changes when a test reads a store\\u0027s files is in scope.\\n\\nNon-goals: no upstream Fisher or Weasel change (a workaround in this repository is fine, and the pull request may name an upstream issue to file); no change to RecordExportTests or StoreDisposalTests beyond what a named cause needs; no new test infrastructure beyond what deterministic reproduction needs; no CI configuration change; not the RepoFieldTests failure.
